    - `is_header` (boolean): whether the structure model recognises the cell as a header cell.
  - The `cells` array must be ordered ascending by `row`, then by `col`.
  - Every grid position in `[0, num_rows) x [0, num_cols)` must be covered by exactly one logical cell (no gaps, no overlaps); consequently the sum of `rowspan * colspan` over all cells equals `num_rows * num_cols`.
- **Normalized HTML table** (`output/table.html`): a **well-formed XML document whose single root element is a `<table>`**. Header cells must be `<th>` elements and body cells `<td>` elements. A cell that spans more than one row must carry a `rowspan` attribute equal to its span, and a cell that spans more than one column must carry a `colspan` attribute equal to its span. The grid encoded by the HTML must be identical to the grid described by `output/grid.json`.
- Where the exact segmentation of an ambiguous merged region admits more than one valid representation, you may choose any internally-consistent convention, provided every invariant above (grid dimensions, full non-overlapping coverage, spanning-header spans, and placement of each known value) still holds and the HTML and JSON agree.

81:T1e33,# Teach Docling a New Input Format (RCP/1.0)

## Background

Docling is preinstalled in this container (`import docling`, distribution `docling-slim` 2.115.0, `docling-core` 2.87.1, Python 3.12) together with all of its model weights. **The container has no network access**: nothing may be downloaded, and no external or cloud service may be contacted. Only preinstalled packages may be used.

A lab publishes its protocols in a small in-house plain-text format called **RCP/1.0** (`.rcp`). Downstream teams want those protocols in the same document model, exports and chunk stream that Docling already produces for its natively supported formats, so RCP must become a first-class Docling input format rather than a side-channel parser.

## The RCP/1.0 format

An RCP file is UTF-8 text with LF line endings and is read line by line.

1. The **first line** must be exactly `%RCP/1.0`.
2. Then comes the **header block**: every line has the form `<key>=<value>`, where `<key>` matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` and `<value>` is the rest of the line with surrounding whitespace stripped. The header block ends at the first line that is exactly `%%`. Keys `id` and `title` are required and must have a non-empty value; other keys are allowed and carry no meaning. A repeated key is an error.
3. Everything after the `%%` line is the **body**. Blank lines (empty or whitespace-only) carry no content; they only terminate the block they follow. Every other body line must be exactly one of:
   * `S<n>> <text>` with `<n>` in `1`..`6` — a section heading of level `<n>`.
   * `P> <text>` — a paragraph.
   * `N> <text>` — an ordered step. A run of consecutive `N>` lines is one ordered list.
   * `B> <text>` — a bullet. A run of consecutive `B>` lines is one unordered list.
   * `A> <text>` — an annotation.
   * `F> <ref> :: <caption>` — a figure reference with a caption.
   * A line starting with `|` — one table row. A run of consecutive table-row lines is one table. The cells of a row are obtained by dropping the leading `|`, then dropping one trailing `|` if present, then splitting on `|` and stripping each cell. The first row of a table is its column-header row, and every row of the same table must yield the same number of cells.

A file that violates any rule above (bad magic line, malformed or unterminated header, repeated header key, missing/empty `id` or `title`, unrecognized body line, ragged table) is **malformed**.

## Requirements

Fixtures live under `/home/user/project/corpus` (`clean/`, `mixed/`, `malformed/`, `unsupported/`); they are inputs, not templates for your output.

### 1. RCP as a Docling input format

Docling's own conversion entry point must handle `.rcp` inputs. Expose `build_converter()` in `/home/user/project/rcp_plugin.py`; it must return a `docling.document_converter.DocumentConverter` instance that:

* converts `.rcp` documents given as a filesystem path **and** as an in-memory Docling document stream named `<something>.rcp`, reporting conversion success and returning a Docling document;
* still converts natively supported Markdown (`.md`) documents successfully through the same converter instance;
* reports a conversion **failure** status for a malformed `.rcp` file instead of letting an exception escape, when the caller asks for errors not to be raised;
* does **not** report success for any other input format (e.g. `.csv`).

A converted RCP document must carry the following structure:

* Its document name is the header `id` value.
* Its body starts with a single title element whose text is the header `title` value.
* Each `S<n>>` line becomes a section-heading element whose heading level equals `<n>` and whose text is the line's text. A heading is nested inside the closest preceding heading of a smaller level (if any); every content element is nested inside the closest preceding heading.
* Each `P>` line becomes a plain text element with that text.
* Each `A>` line becomes a plain text element whose text is exactly `NOTE: ` followed by the annotation text.
* Each run of `N>` lines becomes one enumerated (ordered) list, each run of `B>` lines one non-enumerated list, with one list item per line, in file order, carrying the line's text.
* Each table block becomes one table element with `num_rows` equal to the number of rows in the block, `num_cols` equal to the number of cells per row, cell texts as parsed, and the cells of the first row flagged as column headers.
* Each `F>` line becomes one picture element whose caption text is the caption from that line.
* Nothing else is added to the document.

### 2. Unified batch CLI

`/home/user/project/rcp_convert.py`, run from `/home/user/project` as

```
python rcp_convert.py --input-dir <INPUT_DIR> --output-dir <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

converts a mixed directory in one pass. Both options are required.

* Inputs are the regular files **directly** inside `<INPUT_DIR>` whose name ends in `.rcp` or `.md`, processed in ascending file-name order. Subdirectories and every other file are ignored.
* `<OUTPUT_DIR>` is created when missing and receives:
  * `markdown/<stem>.md` — the Markdown export of the converted document (leading/trailing whitespace is not significant);
  * `json/<stem>.json` — the document's JSON serialization, loadable back into an equivalent Docling document;
  * `chunks.jsonl` — one JSON object per line, produced by Docling's hierarchical chunking of each converted document, in chunker order, grouped per input file in the same ascending file-name order. Each object has exactly the keys `file` (input file name), `chunk_index` (integer, restarting at 0 for each input file), `headings` (list of strings, the chunk's heading path, empty when there is none), `text` (the chunk text) and `num_chars` (integer, the number of characters in `text`);
  * `summary.json` — a JSON object with exactly the keys `schema_version` (integer `1`), `counts` and `documents`. `counts` has exactly the keys `total`, `succeeded` and `failed` (integers). `documents` is a list, ordered by `file` ascending, with one object per input file having exactly the keys `file` (file name), `format` (`"rcp"` or `"md"`), `status` (`"success"` or `"failure"`), `num_headings` (number of section-heading elements in the converted document), `num_list_items` (number of list items), `num_tables`, `num_pictures`, `num_chunks` (number of chunk objects written for this file) and `sha256` (lowercase hex SHA-256 of the input file's bytes).
* A file that fails to convert gets `"status": "failure"`, zeros in all five numeric fields, no `markdown/` or `json/` output and no line in `chunks.jsonl`; the run still processes every other file.
* The last line printed on stdout is exactly `converted=<succeeded> failed=<failed> total=<total>`.
* Exit code `0` when every input converted, `1` when at least one input failed to convert, `2` when `<INPUT_DIR>` does not exist or is not a directory (in that case nothing else is required). A Python traceback must never reach stderr.
* Re-running the command with the same input and output directories must rewrite byte-identical output files.

## Implementation Hints

* Project path: `/home/user/project`; both `rcp_plugin.py` and `rcp_convert.py` live directly in it, and `rcp_plugin` must be importable as a top-level module with `/home/user/project` on `sys.path`.
* Command: `python rcp_convert.py --input-dir <INPUT_DIR> --output-dir <OUTPUT_DIR>`, run with `/home/user/project` as the working directory.
* Conversion, exports and chunking must be produced by Docling itself from the converted document; hand-written Markdown/JSON/chunk emitters that bypass Docling's conversion entry point are not acceptable.
* Everything must run offline on CPU.

82:Ted7,# DocTags Round-Trip Fidelity Pipeline (Docling)

## Background
Docling (`docling` **v2.107.0**) parses documents into a unified `DoclingDocument` model and can serialize that model to its native **DocTags** representation, a compact tag-based format designed to losslessly carry document structure (headings, paragraphs, tables, and pictures). A serialization format is only trustworthy if it can be parsed back into an equivalent document. Your job is to build a command-line pipeline that proves this by performing a full **round trip** on a fixture PDF and quantifying whether the reconstructed document is structurally equivalent to the original.

All AI models are pre-baked into the image and the pipeline must run **fully offline** (no network access at runtime).

## Requirements
Build a CLI program that, given one PDF:
1. Converts the PDF into a `DoclingDocument` (the **original** document).
2. Serializes the original document to the **DocTags** representation and writes it verbatim to a fixed file.
3. **Reconstructs** a brand-new `DoclingDocument` by parsing that DocTags file back in (the **reconstructed** document). The reconstructed document MUST be produced from the contents of the written DocTags file — not from the original in-memory document object.
4. Re-exports the reconstructed document to Markdown at a fixed path.
5. Emits a JSON comparison report that quantifies structural equivalence between the original and the reconstructed documents.

## Implementation Hints
- Project path: `/home/user/project`
- A fixture PDF already exists at `/home/user/project/assets/report.pdf`. It contains a document title, multiple section headings (including a nested subsection), body paragraphs, one bordered multi-row/multi-column table, and one embedded figure with a caption.
- Command (run from the project path): `python main.py <input_pdf_path>` where `<input_pdf_path>` is a single positional argument giving the path to the PDF to process (e.g. `python main.py assets/report.pdf`).
- On success the program MUST exit with code `0` and create exactly these three artifacts (paths relative to the project path):
  - `out/original.doctags` — the DocTags serialization of the original document, written verbatim (it must contain the DocTags structural tags emitted for the table and for the picture).
  - `out/reconstructed.md` — the Markdown export of the reconstructed document.
  - `out/comparison_report.json` — the comparison report described below.
- If the positional argument is missing, or the referenced file does not exist, the program MUST exit with code `2`, MUST NOT write any artifact under `out/`, and MUST NOT emit a Python traceback.
- The comparison report at `out/comparison_report.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly these top-level keys: `original`, `reconstructed`, `match`, `equivalent`.
  - `original` and `reconstructed` are each an object with exactly the integer keys `texts`, `tables`, `pictures`, `headings`, where:
    - `texts` = the total number of text items in that document.
    - `tables` = the number of table items in that document.
    - `pictures` = the number of picture items in that document.
    - `headings` = the number of section-header items in that document (the document title is NOT a section header and MUST NOT be counted).
  - `match` is an object with exactly the boolean keys `texts`, `tables`, `pictures`, `headings`; each is `true` iff the corresponding count in `original` equals the count in `reconstructed`.
  - `equivalent` is a boolean that is `true` iff all four values in `match` are `true`.
- The counts under `reconstructed` MUST be derived from the reconstructed document (the one parsed back from `out/original.doctags`), so that skipping the parse-back step cannot produce a correct report.

83:T2de4,# Local Asynchronous Document-Conversion Gateway

## Background
A field-operations team needs an internal, fully offline HTTP gateway that turns document conversion into *managed asynchronous jobs*: clients submit documents, poll or stream progress, cancel work, and fetch results in several representations long after the conversion finished — even if the gateway process was restarted in between.

You must build this gateway yourself, from scratch, on top of the pinned `docling` **2.107.0** library that is already installed in this container (its model weights are pre-baked locally). Do **not** use, wrap, proxy, or start any ready-made document conversion server product; the gateway, its queue, its worker model and its durable store are all yours to design and implement.

The container has **no network access at runtime**. Every Python package you need (an ASGI web framework, an ASGI server and an HTTP client library among them) is already installed — do not attempt to install anything.

## Requirements
- Accept conversion jobs from two different submission surfaces: an uploaded file, and a reference to a file already on the local disk.
- Support an idempotency-key contract so that a retried submission never converts the same document twice.
- Run conversions through a bounded worker/queue model with explicit, documented backpressure once the queue is saturated.
- Expose a job state machine with timestamps and progress, plus job listing, cancellation, and a streaming progress feed.
- Serve finished results in three different representations derived from the real conversion.
- Persist job state and results so a restarted gateway keeps serving everything it already finished, and repairs jobs that were interrupted.
- Return structured errors from a fixed error-code taxonomy, and expose health and metrics endpoints.

## Implementation Hints
- Project path: `/home/user/project`
- Start command (run with the project path as the working directory): `python service/main.py`
- The gateway MUST bind **127.0.0.1** only, on the TCP port given by the environment variable `GATEWAY_PORT` (default `8077`), and MUST answer `GET /healthz` with HTTP 200 within 60 seconds of process start. Base URL below: `http://127.0.0.1:${GATEWAY_PORT}`.
- Environment variables the gateway MUST honour:
  - `GATEWAY_PORT` — listen port, default `8077`.
  - `GATEWAY_STATE_DIR` — directory holding all durable state, default `/home/user/project/state`. It MUST be created if missing, and it MUST be the only place durable job data is written.
  - `GATEWAY_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` — per-job wall-clock budget measured from the moment the job starts running, default `120`.
- On `SIGTERM` the process MUST exit within 10 seconds.
- Fixed capacity model: **at most 2 jobs may be in state `running` at any moment**, and **at most 4 accepted-but-not-yet-started jobs may wait** in the queue. Waiting jobs MUST start in ascending `seq` order (FIFO). Serving any HTTP request (including `GET /healthz` and result reads) MUST NOT be blocked by running conversions: `GET /healthz` MUST answer in under 1 second even while both workers are busy and other clients are streaming.

### Job object
Every endpoint that returns a job returns this exact JSON object (all keys always present):

```json
{
  "job_id": "string, canonical UUID, unique per job",
  "seq": "integer, starts at 1, +1 per accepted job, never reused, survives restart",
  "state": "queued | running | succeeded | failed | cancelled",
  "source_kind": "upload | path",
  "source_name": "string, the base file name of the submitted document",
  "fingerprint": "string, lowercase sha256 hex digest of the exact document bytes",
  "pace_seconds": "number",
  "progress": "number in [0.0, 1.0], rounded to 2 decimals",
  "created_at": "RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in Z",
  "started_at": "RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in Z, or null",
  "finished_at": "RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in Z, or null",
  "duration_seconds": "number rounded to 3 decimals = finished_at - started_at, or null when either is null",
  "cancel_requested": "boolean",
  "error": "null, or {\"code\": string, \"message\": non-empty string}"
}
```

Progress rules: exactly `0.0` while `queued`; strictly greater than `0.0` and strictly less than `1.0` while `running`; exactly `1.0` when `succeeded`; any value in `[0.0, 1.0]` when `failed` or `cancelled`.

`pace_seconds` is a client-supplied throttle used for load rehearsals: the worker MUST hold the job in state `running` for that many seconds **before** the conversion begins. That waiting time counts as running time and counts toward `GATEWAY_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Accepted range: `0 <= pace_seconds <= 30`; default `0`.

### Endpoints
- `POST /v1/jobs/upload` — `multipart/form-data` with a required part named `file` (binary, carrying a filename) and an optional part named `pace_seconds`. Optional request header `Idempotency-Key`.
- `POST /v1/jobs/path` — `application/json` body `{"source_path": "<absolute path>", "pace_seconds": <number, optional>}`. Optional request header `Idempotency-Key`. Only paths inside `/home/user/project/assets` may be read; anything else (including paths that merely traverse or point outside it) MUST be refused with `403 PATH_NOT_ALLOWED`, which MUST be decided **before** existence is considered. A permitted path that does not point at an existing regular file MUST yield `404 SOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
- Both submission endpoints return **201** with the job object for a newly accepted job. Neither may reject a submission because of the document's extension, media type, or content: format problems surface as a failed job, never as a rejected submission.
- Idempotency: when `Idempotency-Key` is present and that key was already used, the gateway MUST return **200** with the *original, unchanged* job object and MUST NOT enqueue or perform another conversion; if the replay carries a document whose `fingerprint` differs from the stored one, it MUST fail with `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT` and MUST NOT create a job. Keys are global across both submission endpoints and survive a restart. A submission **without** the header always creates a new job, even for byte-identical content.
- Backpressure: a submission that would exceed the 4-slot queue MUST be rejected with **429** `QUEUE_FULL` and a `Retry-After` response header holding an integer number of seconds `>= 1`. An idempotent replay of a known key MUST still succeed with 200 even while the queue is full.
- `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}` — **200** with the job object, or `404 JOB_NOT_FOUND`.
- `GET /v1/jobs?state=<state>&limit=<n>` — **200** with `{"count": <integer>, "jobs": [<job object>, ...]}`, ordered by `seq` **descending**, `count` equal to the number of returned jobs. `state`, when present, filters to that state and MUST be one of the five states. `limit` is an integer in `[1, 100]`, default `50`. A malformed `state` or `limit` MUST yield `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}/result?format=<markdown|json|chunks>` — `format` defaults to `markdown`; any other value MUST yield `400 INVALID_FORMAT`. Every successful result response MUST carry the response header `X-Job-Id` holding the job id.
  - `markdown` — **200**, `Content-Type` beginning with `text/markdown`, body being the converted document rendered as Markdown.
  - `json` — **200**, `application/json`, body `{"job_id": "...", "format": "json", "document": { ... }}` where `document` is the converted document's own complete structured dictionary representation.
  - `chunks` — **200**, `application/json`, body `{"job_id": "...", "format": "chunks", "count": <integer>, "chunks": [ ... ]}`. Each chunk object has exactly the keys `index` (integer, starting at 0, ascending, contiguous), `text` (non-empty string), `headings` (array of strings — the section-heading trail the chunk sits under, possibly empty, every entry also appearing in the Markdown representation), and `char_len` (integer, equal to the length of `text`). Chunks MUST be produced by document-structure-aware chunking of the converted document, not by slicing raw text, and MUST NOT require downloading any tokenizer or model.
  - Requesting a result for a job in state `queued` or `running` MUST yield `409 JOB_NOT_FINISHED`; for a job in state `failed` or `cancelled`, `409 RESULT_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `POST /v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel` —
  - job is `queued`: **200** with the job object already in state `cancelled`; the conversion MUST never run.
  - job is `running`: **202** with the job object, `cancel_requested` set to `true`. If the job is still inside its `pace_seconds` window the conversion MUST NOT start and the job MUST end in state `cancelled`; in any case the job MUST reach a terminal state within 15 seconds of the request.
  - job already terminal: `409 JOB_ALREADY_TERMINAL`.
- `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}/events` — a newline-delimited JSON stream with `Content-Type` beginning with `application/x-ndjson`. Each line is one JSON object with exactly the keys `seq` (integer, starting at 0 and incrementing by 1 per line **within this stream**), `job_id`, `state`, `progress`, and `ts` (RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in `Z`). The first line MUST be emitted within 2 seconds and MUST reflect the job's current state; a new line MUST be emitted whenever `state` or `progress` changes; `progress` MUST never decrease; and the stream MUST end by itself right after emitting a line whose `state` is terminal (so an already-terminal job yields exactly one line and then the response ends). An unknown job id MUST yield `404 JOB_NOT_FOUND` as a normal JSON error response.
- `GET /healthz` — **200** with `{"status": "ok", "workers": 2, "queue_capacity": 4, "queue_depth": <integer>, "running": <integer>, "uptime_seconds": <number>}`.
- `GET /metrics` — **200** with exactly the integer-valued keys `submitted`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `rejected_queue_full`, `idempotent_hits`, `queued_now`, `running_now`. `submitted` counts every accepted job ever (idempotent replays excluded); `succeeded`, `failed` and `cancelled` count jobs currently in those terminal states; these four MUST be derived from the durable store and therefore survive a restart. `rejected_queue_full` and `idempotent_hits` are per-process counters that reset on restart. `queued_now` and `running_now` are the current queue depth and running count.

### Errors
Every response with a status code outside 2xx MUST have `Content-Type: application/json` and the body `{"error": {"code": "<CODE>", "message": "<non-empty string>"}}`, using only these codes: `VALIDATION_ERROR` (400), `INVALID_FORMAT` (400), `PATH_NOT_ALLOWED` (403), `SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (404), `JOB_NOT_FOUND` (404), `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT` (409), `JOB_NOT_FINISHED` (409), `RESULT_UNAVAILABLE` (409), `JOB_ALREADY_TERMINAL` (409), `QUEUE_FULL` (429). A missing `file` part, a missing/blank `source_path`, a non-numeric `pace_seconds`, or a `pace_seconds` outside `[0, 30]` are all `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

Job-level failures are reported in the job object's `error` field with one of exactly these codes: `CONVERSION_FAILED` (the document could not be converted), `JOB_TIMEOUT` (the running budget was exceeded), `INTERRUPTED` (the job was still `queued` or `running` when the process stopped).

### Durability
All job records, idempotency keys and finished results MUST outlive the process. After a restart with the same `GATEWAY_STATE_DIR`, previously `succeeded` jobs MUST still be listable and MUST still serve all three result representations byte-for-byte, and every job that was persisted as `queued` or `running` MUST be repaired at startup into state `failed` with `error.code` `INTERRUPTED` and a non-null `finished_at`.

86:T1fa5,# Token-Budget-Aware Chunk Packing for Retrieval

## Background
An offline retrieval service must ingest a small heterogeneous document corpus and turn it into
embedding-ready chunks. Every chunk has to stay inside a hard token budget of the embedding model,
must carry its section context and provenance, and the whole artifact has to be byte-for-byte
reproducible so that downstream index builds can be cached.

The container is fully air-gapped. Docling is pre-installed (CPU only, all model weights baked into
the image) and a HuggingFace tokenizer directory is baked in as well. Do not install packages,
download models, or contact any network service.

## Requirements
Build a single-file command line tool `chunkpack.py` that converts, chunks, and audits the local
corpus:

- Convert every supported source document in the corpus and split it into chunks whose size is
  governed by a token budget measured with the baked-in tokenizer.
- Emit one contextualized chunk record per line into a JSONL artifact, plus an aggregate summary.
- Guarantee the budget: no emitted chunk may exceed it, including documents that contain a single
  element far larger than the budget, deeply nested section hierarchies, and tables.
- Never drop content: every whitespace-separated word of a document's textual content (including
  table cell values) must appear in that document's emitted chunk texts.
- Expose a self-audit subcommand that re-validates an existing artifact directory.

## Implementation Hints
- Project path: `/home/user/chunkforge`. Create `chunkpack.py` there.
- Corpus (read-only input, do not modify or add files): `/home/user/chunkforge/assets/corpus`.
- Tokenizer: `/home/user/chunkforge/assets/tokenizer`. This local directory is the only tokenizer
  allowed; all token counting must be done with it.
- Commands (always run with the project path as the working directory):
  - `python3 chunkpack.py pack --corpus <dir> --out <dir> --max-tokens <int> [--no-merge-peers]`
  - `python3 chunkpack.py verify --out <dir>`
- `--corpus`, `--out` and `--max-tokens` are mandatory for `pack`. `--no-merge-peers` is optional:
  by default undersized neighbouring chunks that share the same section context are merged together
  while staying inside the budget; when the flag is given that merging must be switched off.
- Source discovery: search `--corpus` recursively. Supported extensions (case-insensitive):
  `.md`, `.html`, `.docx`, `.pdf`. Every other file is ignored for chunking and recorded as skipped.
  A source is identified by its POSIX relative path with respect to the `--corpus` directory
  (e.g. `appendix/omega_notes.md`). All source orderings are ascending by that string.
- `pack` writes exactly two artifacts into `--out` (creating the directory when missing and
  replacing any previous content of these two files): `chunks.jsonl` and `summary.json`.
- `chunks.jsonl` is UTF-8, LF-terminated (no carriage returns), one JSON object per line, with a
  trailing newline after the last object. Chunks are grouped per source in ascending source order,
  and inside a source they keep the order in which the document is read. Each object has exactly
  these nine keys:
  - `chunk_id` (string): `"<source>#<ordinal>"` where `<ordinal>` is zero-padded to 4 digits
    (e.g. `alpha_guide.md#0003`).
  - `index` (integer): 0-based position of the chunk within the whole run; the values on the lines
    must be `0, 1, 2, ...` in ascending order.
  - `source` (string): POSIX relative path of the source document.
  - `ordinal` (integer): 0-based position of the chunk within its own source document.
  - `heading_path` (array of non-empty strings): the section-title ancestry of the chunk, outermost
    title first; an empty array when the chunk has no section context.
  - `page_numbers` (array of integers): ascending, duplicate-free page numbers the chunk's content
    comes from; an empty array when the source format carries no page provenance.
  - `token_count` (integer): the number of tokens the baked-in tokenizer produces for the value of
    `text` (plain tokenization, no special/added tokens counted).
  - `is_partial_element` (boolean): `true` when the chunk carries only a portion of one single
    source element whose content had to be divided across several chunks to respect the budget,
    `false` otherwise.
  - `text` (string): the contextualized chunk text. When `heading_path` is non-empty the text must
    begin with those headings, one per line and in order, followed by a newline and then the chunk
    body; the body must not be empty or whitespace-only. When `heading_path` is empty the text is
    the body alone.
- Budget rule: for every emitted chunk `0 < token_count <= --max-tokens`, without exception. You may
  assume that for the provided corpus and any budget of at least 32 tokens the heading prefix plus
  one body word always fits.
- `summary.json` is UTF-8 JSON with exactly these top-level keys:
  - `tokenizer_path` (string): absolute path of the tokenizer directory used.
  - `max_tokens` (integer): the budget of this run.
  - `merge_peers` (boolean): whether peer merging was active in this run.
  - `documents` (array): one object per successfully chunked source, ascending by `source`, each
    with exactly the keys `source` (string), `chunk_count` (integer), `token_total` (integer, sum of
    the document's `token_count` values), `max_chunk_tokens` (integer, 0 when the document produced
    no chunk), `mean_chunk_tokens` (number, `token_total / chunk_count` rounded to 2 decimals, 0.0
    when the document produced no chunk), `partial_chunk_count` (integer, number of chunks of that
    document with `is_partial_element` true), `max_heading_depth` (integer, longest `heading_path`
    of that document, 0 when none), `page_numbers` (array of integers, ascending duplicate-free
    union of the document's chunk page numbers).
  - `totals` (object) with exactly the keys `document_count`, `chunk_count`, `token_total`,
    `partial_chunk_count` and `budget_violations`, all integers; `budget_violations` counts emitted
    chunks whose `token_count` exceeds `max_tokens` and must therefore be 0.
  - `skipped_files` (array of strings): ascending POSIX relative paths of corpus files ignored
    because of an unsupported extension.
- On success `pack` exits 0 and the last non-empty line it writes to stdout is exactly
  `PACKED documents=<D> chunks=<C> max_tokens=<M> merge_peers=<true|false>` with `<D>`, `<C>` and
  `<M>` matching the summary and the boolean spelled in lowercase.
- `verify --out <dir>` re-reads `<dir>/chunks.jsonl` together with `<dir>/summary.json` (taking the
  budget and the tokenizer location from the summary) and re-checks: valid JSON lines carrying
  exactly the nine required keys; `token_count` equal to a freshly computed token count of `text`;
  `token_count` within the budget; `index` values forming `0..N-1` in ascending order; per-source
  ordinals forming `0..k-1` in ascending order; and `chunk_id` matching the `source`/`ordinal`
  spelling. When everything holds it exits 0 and writes a line starting with `VERIFIED` to stdout.
  When at least one check fails it exits 3, writes nothing containing `VERIFIED` to stdout, and
  writes at least one line starting with `VIOLATION` to stderr.
- Failure handling: exit code 2 with a message beginning with `ERROR` on stderr when the `--corpus`
  directory does not exist, when `--max-tokens` is not an integer of at least 32, or when `verify`
  is pointed at a directory that lacks `chunks.jsonl` or `summary.json`. Exit codes 0, 2 and 3 are
  the only ones the tool may return.
- Determinism: two runs of the same command must produce byte-identical `chunks.jsonl` and
  `summary.json`; nothing time-, host- or randomness-dependent may appear in the artifacts.
- Finally, run the tool once and leave its artifacts in the repository:
  `python3 chunkpack.py pack --corpus assets/corpus --out out --max-tokens 128`
  so that `/home/user/chunkforge/out/chunks.jsonl` and `/home/user/chunkforge/out/summary.json`
  exist and are up to date.

- Command: `python3 audit.py`
- Options (all optional, exact spelling):
  - `--corpus <dir>` (default `corpus`)
  - `--out <dir>` (default `out`)
  - `--max-iterations <int>` (default `3`, valid range 2..10 inclusive)
  - `--min-similarity <float>` (default `0.95`, valid range 0.0..1.0 inclusive)
  - `--doc <document_id>` — repeatable; when present, restricts the audit to exactly the listed document ids
- Relative path arguments resolve against the current working directory.

### Corpus and document ids
- Eligible source files are the regular files located directly inside the corpus directory (no recursion) whose lowercased extension is `.md` or `.html`. Every other entry is ignored.
- A document id is the source file name without its extension.
- The invocation is invalid (exit `2`, see "Gate and exit codes") when: the corpus path does not exist or is not a directory; no eligible file is found; two eligible files share the same document id; or a `--doc` value is not among the eligible document ids.

### Channels and the iterated cycle
- The channels are exactly `json` and `markdown`. The `json` channel uses Docling's lossless JSON serialization of the document model, the `markdown` channel uses Markdown. Their artifact extensions are `.json` and `.md`.
- `D0` is the document model parsed from the source file. For iteration `i` (1-based): `T_i` is the channel serialization of `D_(i-1)` as text, and `D_i` is the document model parsed back from `T_i`. Every run performs exactly `--max-iterations` (`K`) iterations, producing `T_1 .. T_K`, regardless of early convergence.
- Every `T_i` is written UTF-8 encoded to `<out>/documents/<document_id>/<channel>/iter_<NN>.<ext>`, where `NN` is the iteration number zero-padded to two digits.
- Independently of the cycles, `D0` is exported to HTML exactly once per document and written UTF-8 encoded to `<out>/documents/<document_id>/observation.html`. This is an observation only: it never takes part in a cycle, a classification or the gate.

### Normalized text
`normalize(s)` is defined as, in this exact order: (1) apply Unicode NFC; (2) replace every `CR LF` and then every remaining `CR` with `LF`; (3) replace every TAB (U+0009) and every NO-BREAK SPACE (U+00A0) with one SPACE (U+0020); (4) split into lines on `LF`; (5) in every line collapse each run of two or more SPACE characters into one SPACE, then strip leading and trailing SPACE characters; (6) drop the lines that are empty at this point; (7) join the surviving lines with a single `LF`.

### Similarity
`similarity(a, b)` operates on `normalize(a)` and `normalize(b)`: split both on whitespace into the token lists `A` and `B`; when both are empty the value is `1.0`; otherwise the value is `2 * S / (len(A) + len(B))` where `S` is the sum, over the distinct tokens `t`, of `min(count of t in A, count of t in B)`. Every similarity value that is stored or printed is rounded to 6 decimal places, half away from zero.

### Structure signature
The structure signature of a document model is an object with exactly these keys:
- `item_counts`: object mapping a label to the number of content items carrying it, counting every content item reachable from the document body. A key is the label the document model reports for the item, lowercased, with every character outside `[a-z0-9]` replaced by `_`. Labels with no occurrence are omitted.
- `max_depth`: integer; the greatest depth reached in the body tree, where the direct children of the body root have depth 1, and `0` when the body has no children.
- `table_dims`: array of `[rows, cols]` integer pairs, one per table of the document, in document order.

### Per-iteration record
For every iteration `i` record an object with exactly these keys: `iteration` (int, 1-based), `bytes` (int, the byte length of the UTF-8 encoded `T_i`), `sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the UTF-8 encoded `T_i`), `normalized_sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the UTF-8 encoded `normalize(T_i)`), `byte_equal_to_previous` (bool, `T_i` equals `T_(i-1)` byte for byte), `normalized_equal_to_previous` (bool, `normalize(T_i)` equals `normalize(T_(i-1))`), `similarity_to_previous` (number, `similarity(T_i, T_(i-1))`), `structure` (the structure signature of `D_i`) and `structure_equal_to_previous` (bool, the structure signature of `D_i` equals the one of `D_(i-1)`). Iteration 1 has no previous iteration: its three booleans are `false` and its `similarity_to_previous` is `0.0`.

### Fixpoint and classification
- `fixpoint_iteration` is the smallest `i` in `1..K-1` for which `T_i` equals `T_(i+1)` byte for byte, and `null` when there is none. `converged` is `true` exactly when `fixpoint_iteration` is not `null`.
- Every run gets exactly one code; the first matching rule wins, and "final record" means the record whose `iteration` equals `K`:
  1. `fixpoint_iteration` is `1` → `STABLE_IMMEDIATE`
  2. `fixpoint_iteration` is not `null` → `STABLE_DELAYED`
  3. the final record's `normalized_equal_to_previous` is `true` → `WHITESPACE_DRIFT`
  4. the final record's `structure_equal_to_previous` is `true` → `TEXT_DRIFT`
  5. otherwise → `STRUCTURE_DRIFT`
- The `final_similarity` of a run is the final record's `similarity_to_previous`.

### Gate and exit codes
Walk the runs in report order (document id ascending, then channel ascending) and append to `violations`: first `<document_id>/<channel>:<code>` when the code is neither `STABLE_IMMEDIATE` nor `STABLE_DELAYED`, then `<document_id>/<channel>:LOW_SIMILARITY` when `final_similarity` is lower than `--min-similarity`. The gate passes exactly when `violations` is empty.
- exit `0`: the audit completed and the gate passed.
- exit `3`: the audit completed and the gate failed; every artifact is still written in full.
- exit `2`: the invocation is invalid — the corpus/`--doc` cases listed above, or `--max-iterations` / `--min-similarity` outside their valid range or not parseable as the required type. Then nothing at all is printed on stdout, stderr carries at least one line that starts with `error: ` (this also applies to argument-parsing failures, so the default parser diagnostics are not sufficient on their own), and the output directory and its contents are neither created, deleted nor modified.

### Output artifacts
On a valid invocation the tool first removes all existing contents of the output directory (creating that directory when it is missing), then writes:
- `<out>/report.json`
- `<out>/summary.txt`
- `<out>/documents/<document_id>/detail.json`
- `<out>/documents/<document_id>/observation.html`
- `<out>/documents/<document_id>/<channel>/iter_<NN>.<ext>`

`report.json` and every `detail.json` are UTF-8 encoded, indented with 2 spaces, have their object keys sorted ascending at every nesting level, leave non-ASCII characters unescaped (a document id carrying non-ASCII characters therefore appears verbatim), and end with exactly one newline character. The iteration artifacts of the `json` channel are not constrained beyond being the channel's own serialization.

`report.json` is an object with exactly these keys:
- `schema_version`: the string `1.0`
- `corpus`: the absolute, resolved path of the corpus directory
- `max_iterations`: int
- `min_similarity`: number
- `channels`: the array `["json", "markdown"]`
- `documents`: array ordered by `document_id` ascending; every entry has exactly `document_id` (string), `source_file` (the source file name including its extension), `html_sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the observation HTML bytes) and `runs`
- every entry of `runs` has exactly `channel`, `iterations` (int, equal to `max_iterations`), `fixpoint_iteration` (int or `null`), `converged` (bool), `code` (string) and `final_similarity` (number), ordered by `channel` ascending
- `totals`: exactly `documents` (int), `runs` (int), `converged_runs` (int), `codes` (object carrying all five codes as keys and their run counts as values) and `min_final_similarity` (number, the smallest `final_similarity` over all runs)
- `gate`: exactly `passed` (bool), `exit_code` (int, the process exit code) and `violations` (array of strings)

`<out>/documents/<document_id>/detail.json` is an object with exactly the keys `document_id`, `source_file`, `source_sha256` (lowercase hex digest of the source file bytes), `html_sha256`, `html_bytes` (int, byte length of the observation HTML) and `channels`. `channels` is an object keyed by channel name whose values have exactly the keys `code`, `converged`, `fixpoint_iteration`, `final_similarity`, `artifacts` (array of the iteration artifact paths relative to the document directory, in iteration order) and `iterations` (array of the per-iteration records, in iteration order).

### summary.txt and stdout
`summary.txt` is UTF-8 encoded with LF line endings and has exactly `9 + R` lines, `R` being the number of runs:
- line 1: `FIXPOINT AUDIT`
- line 2: `corpus: <absolute corpus path>`
- line 3: `documents: <number of audited documents>`
- line 4: `runs: <number of runs>`
- line 5: `max_iterations: <int>`
- line 6: `min_similarity: <value with exactly 6 decimals>`
- line 7: empty
- lines 8 .. 7+R: one line per run in report order, formatted as `<document_id> <channel> <code> fixpoint=<n> similarity=<value>` with single spaces between the five fields, `<n>` being the fixpoint iteration or `-` when there is none, and `<value>` the final similarity with exactly 6 decimals
- line 8+R: empty
- line 9+R: `GATE: PASS` when the gate passed, otherwise `GATE: FAIL (<v> violations)` with `<v>` the number of violations

The file ends with exactly one newline character. On exit `0` and exit `3` stdout must be byte-identical to the contents of `summary.txt`; any diagnostics belong on stderr.

### Determinism
Re-running the tool with the same corpus and the same options must produce byte-identical `report.json`, `summary.txt`, `detail.json` and iteration artifacts. Do not embed timestamps, durations, random values, or host-specific paths other than the ones specified above.

89:Tfed,# Reconstruct Multi-Column Human Reading Order from Layout Provenance

## Background
Scientific papers, magazines and reports are frequently typeset in multiple text columns, sometimes mixing full-width spanning elements (a title, a banner) with 2-column body text, and always decorated with running page headers, page footers and page numbers. - For every page, determine how many body text columns the page has, assign each body text element to a column, and order the elements into the correct human reading order: any full-width spanning element first (top-to-bottom), then the entire leftmost column top-to-bottom, then the next column to its right, and so on.
- Running page headers, page footers and standalone page numbers must be excluded from the reconstructed reading order entirely.
- Emit a machine-readable per-page description and a single linearized plain-text rendering of the whole document in true reading order.

## Implementation Hints

- Input document: `assets/report.pdf` (resolved against the project path; already generated).

      - `"column"`: integer, 0-based column index, `0` = leftmost. Full-width spanning elements use column `0`.
      - `"bbox"`: a list of four numbers `[l, t, r, b]` in PDF points using a top-left coordinate origin, so that `l < r` and `t < b` (smaller `t` means higher up the page).
  - `output/reading_order.txt` — a UTF-8 plain-text file: the text of every kept element, taken across all pages in ascending page order and, within each page, in the exact same order as that page's `"elements"` list, joined by a single newline (`\n`) between consecutive elements.
- Ordering invariants that the reconstructed order must satisfy, per page: the `"column"` values in `"elements"` are non-decreasing (all of one column is emitted before any element of a column further right), and within a single column the elements are ordered by increasing `"bbox"` top coordinate (top-to-bottom).
- Every `"bbox"` must lie within its page's dimensions (within a small rounding tolerance).

8b:T11f4,# Two-Pass OCR Gating Pipeline for Docling

## Background
Docling (`docling` v2.107.0, already installed in this offline container) extracts a PDF's embedded programmatic text layer by default and only falls back to optical character recognition (OCR) for pages it recognizes as bitmap scans. This produces two failure modes for real-world documents: (a) pages that are image-only scans yield little or no usable text from the programmatic layer, and (b) pages with broken/non-standard font encodings emit corrupted "mojibake" text. A robust ingestion pipeline must therefore *detect* per-page text corruption and selectively repair only the affected pages with OCR, while leaving clean pages untouched.

You must build a command-line pipeline that performs exactly this two-pass "OCR gating" over a fixed input PDF and emits a repaired Markdown document plus a machine-readable gating report.

The environment is fully offline: all model weights and the Tesseract engine are pre-baked into the image. No network access is available at any point.

## Requirements
- Read the input PDF and, using only its embedded programmatic text layer (no OCR), extract the text of every page (Pass 1).
- For every page, compute a numeric `garble_score` from its Pass-1 text using the exact definition given below, and decide whether the page's programmatic text is unusable and must be repaired via OCR.
- For every page decided to need repair, obtain that page's text a second time such that the text is produced by optical character recognition of the rendered page image rather than the embedded text layer (Pass 2). Pass 2 must use the Tesseract OCR engine with English.
- Produce a final "repaired" Markdown document that uses the programmatic-layer text for clean pages and the OCR text for pages flagged for repair.
- Produce a per-page gating report as JSON.

## Implementation Hints
- Project path: `/home/user/project`
- Input PDF (already present, do not regenerate it): `/home/user/project/assets/source.pdf`
- Command (runnable, no arguments, executed from the project path): `python3 main.py`
- The command must write exactly these two output files:
  - `/home/user/project/output/gating_report.json`
  - `/home/user/project/output/repaired.md`
- Running the command multiple times must be idempotent (each run fully regenerates both output files).

### Exact garble-score definition (must be followed precisely)
For a given page, let `T` be the text obtained from ONLY that page's programmatic text layer (Pass 1, OCR disabled). Let `N` be the number of characters in `T` that are not Unicode whitespace. Let `S` be the number of those `N` characters whose Unicode code point is outside the inclusive printable-ASCII range `U+0020`–`U+007E`. Then:
- `garble_score = S / N`, except that when `N == 0` the `garble_score` is defined to be exactly `1.0`.
- Report each `garble_score` rounded to 4 decimal places.

### Exact gating decision (must be followed precisely)
- `GARBLE_THRESHOLD = 0.30`.
- A page needs OCR repair if and only if `garble_score >= GARBLE_THRESHOLD`.
- Pages needing repair get `text_source = "ocr"`; all other pages get `text_source = "programmatic"`.
- Pass 2 (OCR) must be run only for pages that need repair.

### `output/gating_report.json` schema (exact keys)
A single JSON object:
```json
{
  "source_pdf": "assets/source.pdf",
  "garble_threshold": 0.30,
  "page_count": <int>,
  "pages": [
    {
      "page_no": <int, 1-based, ascending>,
      "garble_score": <float rounded to 4 decimals>,
      "programmatic_char_count": <int, count of non-whitespace chars in the Pass-1 text of this page>,
      "ocr_char_count": <int count of non-whitespace chars in this page's OCR text, or null when OCR was not performed for this page>,
      "text_source": <"programmatic" | "ocr">,
      "needs_ocr": <bool>
    }
  ]
}
```
Invariants that must hold in the report: `page_count` equals `len(pages)`; `pages` are ordered by ascending `page_no` starting at 1; for every page `needs_ocr == (garble_score >= garble_threshold) == (text_source == "ocr")`; `ocr_char_count` is `null` for every `programmatic` page and a non-negative integer for every `ocr` page.

### `output/repaired.md` content
- Concatenate, in ascending page order, each page's chosen text: the programmatic-layer text for `programmatic` pages and the OCR text for `ocr` pages.
- Separate consecutive pages with a single blank line.

## Notes
- The pipeline must run entirely offline using only components already present in the image.
- OCR on CPU is slow; the pipeline may take several minutes to run.

8d:T1326,# Per-Page Layout Provenance Overlay Renderer (Docling)

You are working with **Docling** (`docling` v2.107.0, running fully offline on CPU) inside a container that already has all default layout/table/OCR model weights pre-baked.   - An **overlay manifest JSON** listing every element drawn on that page.

## Implementation Hints

- Input document: `/home/user/docling_overlay/assets/report.pdf` (multi-page, machine-readable). Do not modify it.
- Command: `python3 main.py` (run with the project path as the working directory). Running it must (re)generate all artifacts under `/home/user/docling_overlay/output/`.
- The environment is fully offline: the solution MUST NOT access the network or download any model; rely only on the pre-baked local models.

- **Output file naming** (page numbers are Docling's own 1-based page numbers): for a page numbered `N`, write the overlay image to `output/overlay_page_<N>.png` and the manifest to `output/overlay_page_<N>.json`. Produce exactly one PNG and one JSON per page of the document, and nothing spurious for pages that do not exist.

- **Coordinate convention for manifest boxes**: every bounding box you record is expressed in the overlay image's raster **pixel** space, with the origin at the **top-left** corner, x increasing to the right and y increasing downward. Each box is a list `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` of numbers with `0 <= x0 < x1 <= image_width` and `0 <= y0 < y1 <= image_height`. Boxes must account for the image scale and for any difference between the document/page coordinate origin and the top-left raster origin, so that a recorded box coincides with the element's true location in the rendered page to within **3 pixels** on each edge.
- **Element id / type**: use the element's Docling self-reference string (e.g. `#/texts/4`) as its `id`, and the element's Docling label string as its `type`. Only these six element types are in scope: `text`, `section_header`, `list_item`, `table`, `picture`, `caption`. Elements of any other type must be ignored entirely (no rectangle, no manifest entry).
- **Color mapping** (exact, case-insensitive hex strings) — every element and its drawn rectangle use the color for its type:
  - `text` -> `#1f77b4`
  - `section_header` -> `#d62728`
  - `list_item` -> `#2ca02c`
  - `table` -> `#ff7f0e`
  - `picture` -> `#9467bd`
  - `caption` -> `#8c564b`
  The color assigned to a type must be identical for every element of that type across all pages, and the rectangle drawn on the overlay PNG for an element must be rendered in that same color.
- **Manifest JSON schema**: each `output/overlay_page_<N>.json` is a single JSON object with keys:
  - `page_no`: integer, the Docling page number `N`.
  - `image_width`: integer, the overlay PNG pixel width.
  - `image_height`: integer, the overlay PNG pixel height.
  - `boxes`: an array; each entry is an object with exactly the keys `id` (string), `type` (string, one of the six types), `bbox` (list `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` of numbers in the pixel convention above), and `color` (string hex from the map above).

8e:T1454,# Semantic Section Splitter for a Structured PDF

## Background
A long, multi-section technical report is provided as a programmatic PDF at `assets/report.pdf`. Using Docling (Python package `docling`, version `2.107.0`), parse it into a `DoclingDocument` and split it into one Markdown file per top-level section, together with a hierarchical table of contents and working relative cross-links.

The environment is fully offline: all Docling models are pre-baked into the image and the `DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH` environment variable is already set to the local model cache. Do NOT access the network, download models, or use any remote/VLM service.

## Input document format (contract)
The PDF encodes a multi-level heading hierarchy. Because model-predicted heading levels for PDFs can be flat and unreliable, heading levels are encoded deterministically in the text itself:

- A text line is a **section heading** if and only if it begins with a hierarchical outline number matching the regular expression `^\d+(\.\d+){0,2}\s` (for example `1 Introduction`, `2.1 Data Collection`, `3.2.1 Limitations`).
- The heading **level** is the number of dot-separated integers in that leading outline number: one component -> level 1 (a top-level "H1" section), two components -> level 2, three components -> level 3. Determine the level **only** from the outline number, never from any model-predicted level.
- Every other text block is **body content** and belongs, in reading order, to the most recent heading that precedes it.
- The document also has a single top **title** line that has no outline number; it is NOT a section.

## Requirements
From `assets/report.pdf`, produce everything under an `output/` directory inside the project:
1. One Markdown file per H1 (level-1) section, under `output/sections/`, each containing that section and all of its nested subsections and body content in reading order.
2. A hierarchical `output/toc.json` capturing the full heading tree.
3. A root `output/index.md` plus back/sibling cross-links between files.

## Output contract
- Project path: `/home/user/project`
- Command: `python main.py` (executed with the project path as the working directory) must (re)generate all outputs deterministically from `assets/report.pdf`.

### Slug rule
Define `slug(s)`: lowercase `s`; replace every maximal run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` with a single `-`; then strip any leading and trailing `-`. For example `slug("3.2.1 Limitations")` == `3-2-1-limitations`.

### Section files (`output/sections/`)
- There must be exactly one file per H1 section; the number of section files equals the number of H1 headings in the document.
- Filename: `<NN>-<slug>.md`, where `<NN>` is the 1-based position of the H1 section in document order, zero-padded to two digits, and `<slug>` is `slug(<full H1 heading text>)` (the full heading text includes its outline number).
- The file's first Markdown heading line must be `# <full H1 heading text>`.
- Every descendant subsection heading of that H1 must appear in the file as a Markdown heading, in reading order, with a leading `#`-count equal to its level (level-2 -> `## <full text>`, level-3 -> `### <full text>`), using the full heading text.
- All body content belonging to the H1 section and its descendants must appear in this file, and in no other section file. No body text may be lost or duplicated across the section files.
- The file must contain the following relative Markdown links, written as `[text](target)` where `target` is a path relative to the file's own directory that resolves to an existing file:
  - a link whose text is exactly `Index` and whose target resolves to `output/index.md`;
  - for every section except the first, a link whose text is exactly `Previous` and whose target resolves to the previous H1 section's file;
  - for every section except the last, a link whose text is exactly `Next` and whose target resolves to the next H1 section's file.

### `output/index.md`
- Must contain, in document order, one Markdown link per H1 section, where the link text is exactly the full H1 heading text and the target is `sections/<NN>-<slug>.md` (relative to the `output/` directory) and resolves to the existing section file.

### `output/toc.json`
A JSON object with:
- `title` (string): the document's top title text.
- `sections` (array): the level-1 section nodes, in document order.

Each node is a JSON object with:
- `title` (string): the full heading text (including its outline number).
- `level` (integer): 1, 2, or 3.
- `anchor` (string): `slug(title)`.
- `page_no` (integer): the 1-based page number on which the heading appears.
- `children` (array): the child section nodes (of level = this node's level + 1), in document order; an empty array when there are none.
- `filename` (string): **level-1 nodes ONLY** — the section file path relative to the `output/` directory, i.e. `sections/<NN>-<slug>.md`. Nodes of level 2 or 3 must NOT contain a `filename` key.

The tree must reflect the true nesting implied by the outline numbers: each level-2 section is a child of the level-1 section that precedes it, and each level-3 section is a child of the level-2 section that precedes it.

8f:T2d1f,# Offline Table-Structure Quality Benchmark Harness

## Background
Docling (v2 CPU build, `docling` importable from the system Python, every model weight already baked into the image's local artifact cache) can reconstruct the grid of a table it finds on a PDF page, and its table-structure recognizer exposes two operating modes with different speed/quality trade-offs.

A data-engineering team needs hard numbers before choosing a mode for production: how much quality does the slower mode actually buy on their documents, and how much runtime does it cost? Your job is to build the measurement harness that answers this, scored against a ground-truth corpus that ships with the environment.

**The harness must work fully offline.** No network call, external service or model download may be required at run time - everything comes from local resources - and the whole run must fit inside a 3 GB memory limit.

## The corpus (read-only input)
The corpus lives at `/home/user/tfbench/corpus`. You must not modify, move, delete or regenerate any file in it.

- Every `*.pdf` directly inside `corpus/` is one benchmark document. Its `doc_id` is the file name without the `.pdf` suffix.
- Its ground truth is `corpus/ground_truth/<doc_id>.json` with this shape:

```json
{
  "doc_id": "grid_basic",
  "pdf": "grid_basic.pdf",
  "page_count": 1,
  "tables": [
    {
      "table_index": 0,
      "page_no": 1,
      "num_rows": 5,
      "num_cols": 4,
      "cells": [
        {"row": 0, "col": 0, "row_span": 1, "col_span": 1, "text": "Region", "is_header": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`tables` is ordered by `table_index` (document order). `cells` lists every distinct cell exactly once, identified by its top-left grid position (`row`, `col`, both 0-based) plus its `row_span`/`col_span`; spanned-over positions are not listed again. A cell's `text` may be the empty string.

## Requirements
Build a reproducible benchmark CLI at `/home/user/tfbench/bench.py` that, for each selected document, converts the PDF **once per selected table-structure mode** using the real recognizer (never a heuristic re-parse of the PDF, and never the ground truth), extracts the recognized grids, scores them against the ground truth, and writes JSON reports.

- The two modes must be reported under the exact names `fast` and `accurate`, and both must run with table cell-matching enabled.
- Documents are processed in ascending lexicographic `doc_id` order; when both modes are selected, `fast` is run before `accurate`.
- Reports must be deterministic: two runs with the same arguments must produce byte-identical `docs/*.json`, `aggregate.json` and `comparison.json` (no timestamps, no durations, no absolute paths, no run-dependent ordering inside them). Every JSON file must be UTF-8 and end with a newline.

## Interface
Command: `python3 bench.py [--corpus DIR] [--out DIR] [--doc DOC_ID] [--mode {fast,accurate,both}]`

- `--corpus` defaults to `corpus`, `--out` defaults to `reports`, `--mode` defaults to `both`; relative paths resolve against the current working directory. Omitting `--doc` selects every document in the corpus; `--doc` takes a single `doc_id` and restricts the run to it.
- The output directory (and its `docs/` subdirectory) must be created if missing.

## Scoring rules

**Text normalization** (applied to both ground-truth and recognized cell text, in this order): Unicode NFKC normalization; replace every run of whitespace characters with a single ASCII space; strip leading/trailing spaces; casefold; delete every character that is not a Unicode letter, a Unicode digit, a space, `.` or `-`; replace runs of spaces with a single space again; strip again.

**Table pairing**: for each document, the recognized tables in document order are paired positionally with the ground-truth tables (`table_index` 0 with the 0th recognized table, and so on). A ground-truth table with no counterpart is scored as a total miss (no recognized shape, zero agreements). Recognized tables beyond the ground-truth count are only counted, not scored.

**Cell probing**: a ground-truth cell at (`row`, `col`) is compared with the recognized cell that covers grid position (`row`, `col`) in the paired recognized table — i.e. the cell whose row range and column range both contain that position; if several do, the first one in the recognized table's own cell order wins. If no recognized cell covers the position (including when the recognized grid is smaller), the probe has no recognized counterpart: its recognized text, span and header flag are all `null` and none of its three agreements hold.

**Per-cell agreements**: content matches when the normalized texts are equal (two empty strings match); the span matches when (`row_span`, `col_span`) are pairwise equal; the header flag matches when the ground-truth `is_header` equals whether the recognized table marks that cell as a column-header cell.

**Per-table metrics**: `matched_cells`, `span_agreements` and `header_agreements` are the counts of the corresponding agreements over the ground-truth cells of that table; each rate is that count divided by the table's ground-truth cell count. `shape_match` is true only when the recognized row count and column count both equal the ground-truth ones.

**Aggregation**: corpus-level rates are micro-averaged — the summed agreement counts over all scored tables divided by the summed ground-truth cell count — never the mean of per-table rates. `shape_match_rate` is the number of shape-matching tables divided by the ground-truth table count of the run.

**Rounding**: every rate and every duration written to JSON is a float; rates are rounded to 4 decimals and durations to 3 decimals. A rate whose denominator is 0 is `0.0`.

**Quality gate**: `best_mode` is the selected mode with the highest corpus-level `cell_match_rate` (on a tie, `fast`); `best_cell_match_rate` is its rate. The gate passes when `best_cell_match_rate` is greater than or equal to `0.5`.

## Output files (all under `--out`)

`docs/<doc_id>.json`, one per selected document:

```json
{
  "doc_id": "string",
  "pdf": "string",
  "gt_table_count": 0,
  "gt_cell_count": 0,
  "modes": {
    "fast": {
      "mode": "fast",
      "cell_matching": true,
      "converted": true,
      "error": null,
      "predicted_table_count": 0,
      "unmatched_predicted_tables": 0,
      "tables": [
        {
          "table_index": 0,
          "page_no": 1,
          "gt_shape": [0, 0],
          "pred_shape": [0, 0],
          "shape_match": true,
          "pred_page_no": 1,
          "pred_bbox": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
          "gt_cell_count": 0,
          "matched_cells": 0,
          "cell_match_rate": 0.0,
          "span_agreements": 0,
          "span_match_rate": 0.0,
          "header_agreements": 0,
          "header_match_rate": 0.0,
          "cells": [
            {
              "row": 0,
              "col": 0,
              "gt_text_normalized": "string",
              "pred_text_normalized": "string",
              "matched": true,
              "gt_span": [1, 1],
              "pred_span": [1, 1],
              "span_match": true,
              "gt_header": true,
              "pred_header": true,
              "header_match": true
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

`modes` holds exactly the modes that were run. `error` is `null` on success and otherwise a non-empty string describing the failure, with `converted` false and `tables` still listing every ground-truth table as a total miss. `pred_shape` is `[rows, cols]` or `null`; `pred_page_no` is the 1-based page of the recognized table or `null`; `pred_bbox` is the recognized table's bounding box as `[left, top, right, bottom]` in page coordinates rounded to 2 decimals, or `null`. `tables` is ordered by `table_index` and `cells` by (`row`, `col`) ascending.

`aggregate.json`:

```json
{
  "corpus_dir": "corpus",
  "doc_ids": ["string"],
  "doc_count": 0,
  "gt_table_count": 0,
  "gt_cell_count": 0,
  "modes": {
    "fast": {
      "mode": "fast",
      "cell_matching": true,
      "documents_run": 0,
      "documents_converted": 0,
      "documents_failed": 0,
      "predicted_table_count": 0,
      "shape_match_count": 0,
      "shape_match_rate": 0.0,
      "matched_cells": 0,
      "cell_match_rate": 0.0,
      "span_agreements": 0,
      "span_match_rate": 0.0,
      "header_agreements": 0,
      "header_match_rate": 0.0
    }
  },
  "best_mode": "fast",
  "best_cell_match_rate": 0.0,
  "quality_gate": {"min_cell_match_rate": 0.5, "passed": true}
}
```

`corpus_dir` is the corpus path exactly as it was given on the command line (or its default). `doc_ids` is sorted ascending.

`comparison.json` — written **only** when both modes ran:

```json
{
  "modes": ["fast", "accurate"],
  "tables": [
    {
      "doc_id": "string",
      "table_index": 0,
      "fast_shape": [0, 0],
      "accurate_shape": [0, 0],
      "shape_differs": false,
      "fast_cell_match_rate": 0.0,
      "accurate_cell_match_rate": 0.0,
      "cell_match_rate_delta": 0.0,
      "differing_cells": [[0, 0]],
      "differing_cell_count": 0,
      "verdict": "tie"
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "tables_compared": 0,
    "accurate_better": 0,
    "fast_better": 0,
    "tie": 0,
    "shape_differs_count": 0
  }
}
```

One entry per ground-truth table, ordered by (`doc_id`, `table_index`) ascending. `differing_cells` lists the (`row`, `col`) probes whose normalized recognized text differs between the two modes (a `null` differs from any string; two `null`s do not), sorted ascending; `cell_match_rate_delta` is the accurate rate minus the fast rate rounded to 4 decimals, and `verdict` is `accurate_better`, `fast_better` or `tie` according to that delta's sign.

`timing.json` — this file is the only one exempt from the byte-identical requirement:

```json
{

    "fast": {
      "documents": 0,
      "total_seconds": 0.0,
      "mean_seconds_per_document": 0.0,
      "min_seconds": 0.0,
      "max_seconds": 0.0
    }
  },
  "total_seconds": 0.0
}
```

Per-mode values are measured over the per-document conversion+scoring work of that mode (documents that failed to convert still count in `documents`); `total_seconds` at the top level is the wall-clock duration of the whole run and is therefore at least as large as any mode's `total_seconds`.

## Process contract
- The last non-empty line of stdout must be exactly `GATE <PASS|FAIL> best_mode=<mode> cell_match_rate=<rate>`, where `<rate>` is `best_cell_match_rate` formatted with exactly 4 decimals. Diagnostics belong on stderr.
- Exit codes: `0` — everything ran and the gate passed. `3` — everything ran but the gate failed. `4` — selection/corpus error: `--doc` names an unknown document, a discovered PDF has no ground-truth file, or there is nothing to run; in this case a non-empty message goes to stderr, no `GATE` line is printed, and **no file inside the output directory may be created or modified**. `5` — at least one selected document failed to convert; the remaining documents are still processed and all reports are still written. `2` — invalid command-line usage. When several apply, the highest-priority code wins in the order `4`, `5`, `3`, `0`.

## Deliverable
Besides the harness itself, leave a complete full-corpus run in place: `/home/user/tfbench/reports/` must contain the reports produced by `python3 bench.py` run with default arguments (all documents, both modes) from `/home/user/tfbench`.

- Project path: `/home/user/tfbench`

a3:T166e,# Overlapping Gravity Fields with Space-Override Priority Resolution

## Background

In Godot 4, several `Area2D` nodes can overlap and each can override gravity for
bodies inside it. Each area has a gravity **space-override mode**, a **priority**,
and either a **directional** or a **point** gravity definition. When a point is
covered by multiple areas, the engine resolves a single net gravity vector by
processing the overlapping areas in priority order and combining/replacing their
contributions according to each area's override mode, optionally folding in the
project's default gravity.

You must build a Godot 4 project that (a) reproduces this resolution logic for an
arbitrary world position and (b) contains a real `RigidBody2D` that falls through
the configured fields with the correct resulting trajectory.

## Requirements

- Build a scene containing six overlapping `Area2D` gravity fields (exactly as
  specified below) plus one `RigidBody2D` probe.
- Implement a controller that, given any world-space position, returns the net
  gravity vector that Godot's `Area2D` space-override rules (together with the
  project's default gravity) produce at that position.
- The `RigidBody2D` probe must respond to these fields so that, starting from a
  known rest state and advancing Godot's fixed-step physics, it reaches the
  expected position and velocity at the specified checkpoints.

## Implementation Hints

- Project path: `/home/user/gravity_fields` (an empty, valid Godot 4 project is
